## Section 10: Main-text figures {.page-break-before}

::: {.content-visible when-profile="docs"}
Sections 2–9 document the analyses in full. This section collects the figures that appear in the **main manuscript**, which present a deliberately reduced selection of those results for a general readership. It exists so that every main-text figure has exactly one authoritative definition.

**How this section works.**

-   Each main figure appears **once**, embedded from `figures/main/`, with its **full build code in the collapsible drop-down** beneath it (HTML version).
-   Every figure is written in three formats to the same stem: **`.png` and `.jpg` at 600 dpi** (raster, for whichever a submission system demands) and **`.pdf`** (vector, for print). The appendix embeds the PNG.
-   That code chunk **is the source of truth** for the figure. There is no parallel copy in `Scripts/`; nothing else generates these files.
-   The chunks are `eval: false`, so rendering this appendix never rebuilds a figure. To rebuild one after editing its chunk, run the runner from the `Supplementary/` directory:

``` bash
conda run -n r_env Rscript build_main_figure.R fig1-build
```

-   Each figure carries a one-line **provenance cross-reference** naming the thematic sections its inputs come from.
-   The thematic sections keep their own supplementary version of a plot only where it is genuinely different (a different object, more ranks, unfiltered); where it would be the same object, they cross-reference here instead.

**File-naming rule.** Supplementary figure files begin with `S`; main-text figure files are `Fig<N>_<slug>` and live in `figures/main/`. (One legacy exception is pending: `figures/Fig1_guild_season.png` is the *supplementary* Figure S-GUILDa of Section 8 and is scheduled for renaming.)
:::

### 10.1 Figure 1 — Composition and function of the dung mycobiome

:::: {.content-visible when-profile="docs"}
*Provenance: Fig. 1A uses the genus-level composition of Section 3.1 and Fig. 1B the guild assignments of Section 8.2, both on the canonical 52-sample object (`alldat$nopool`) and on one shared sample axis. The season test once drawn as panel C is Figure S-GUILDa(B) of Section 8.2 (same rule, same test; the build chunk re-checks its q-values against `tables/guild_season_readshare.csv`).*
::::

![](figures/main/Fig1_composition_function.png)

**Figure 1**: Composition and function of the willow ptarmigan dung mycobiome in winter and summer. **(A)** Per-dropping read share of the nine most abundant genera, all other named genera (*Other genera*) and reads on OTUs with no confident genus assignment (*No genus: dark taxa*), for 26 winter and 26 summer droppings; the right-hand bar of each season is the mean over its droppings, labelled in % for segments of at least 8%. **(B)** Per-dropping read share of five functional guilds for the same droppings in the same order (within each season, descending dung-saprotroph share). Each genus in (A) is drawn in a shade of its guild's colour in (B), as the key shows; thin white borders separate the segments. The seasonal test of each guild is Figure S-GUILDa(B) (Appendix Section 8.2).

:::: {.content-visible when-profile="docs"}
*Narrative carried over from the previous Figure 1, whose panel C was the guild × season boxplot now cited as Figure S-GUILDa(B); to be rewritten for the new figure.*

Read down a column and the two descriptions line up: the summer samples that are almost entirely dung saprotrophs in (B) are the samples dominated end-to-end by *Thelebolus*, *Sporormiella* and *Coniochaeta* in (A), while winter samples are a patchwork of many low-abundance genera sitting under a large unassigned fraction. The seasonal contrast is therefore the same result seen taxonomically and functionally: dung saprotrophs rise from 13.6% of winter reads to 51.5% in summer, and the unassigned fraction falls from 51.1% to 21.0% (panel C; Section 8.2). Panel A also makes the interpretive limit visible — roughly half of a typical winter sample is reads that carry no genus at all, which is the subject of the dark-taxa analysis in Section 3.4.
::::

```{r fig1-build}
#| eval: false
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Full build code for Figure 1 — the source of truth for figures/main/Fig1_composition_function.{png,jpg,pdf}"

# Figure 1 -- Composition and function of the dung mycobiome.
# Journal layout: 174 mm double column, 7-8 pt text.
# Canonical object alldat$nopool (52 samples). Panels A and B share one sample
# axis and one key. (The proposed-pathway schematic once drawn as panel C was
# removed on 2026-11-23, to be reworked as a separate introductory figure; its
# code is in git history, e.g. commit f744dbb.)
# Rebuild:  conda run -n r_env Rscript build_main_figure.R fig1-build

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(phyloseq); library(ggplot2); library(patchwork)
})

rdata <- if (file.exists("eco_analysis.RData")) "eco_analysis.RData" else
         "/home/daniel/Ptarmigan/trimmed/mergedPlates/eco_analysis.RData"
load(rdata)
stopifnot(exists("alldat"), exists("funguild_otu"))   # funguild_otu <- 8_functional_guilds.R

out_dir <- "figures/main"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
grDevices::pdf(NULL)                                  # headless: no X11 fallback

# ---- data ------------------------------------------------------------------
ps  <- alldat$nopool                                  # 52 samples, PCR reps summed
m   <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix"); if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) m <- t(m)   # samples x taxa
rel <- m / rowSums(m)
stopifnot(all(abs(rowSums(rel) - 1) < 1e-10))

md     <- data.frame(as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
Season <- factor(c(winter = "Winter", summer = "Summer")[md$Season],
                 levels = c("Winter", "Summer"))
stopifnot(!anyNA(Season), identical(rownames(rel), rownames(m)))

strip_rank <- function(x) sub("^[a-z]__", "", x)      # "g__Sporormiella" -> "Sporormiella"
tax <- data.frame(as(tax_table(ps), "matrix"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
gen <- strip_rank(tax$Genus[match(colnames(m), rownames(tax))])
gen <- ifelse(gen %in% c("", "NA"), NA, gen)

# ---- panel A categories: top genera + Other + Unassigned -------------------
N_GENERA  <- 9                                        # see the palette note below
by_genus  <- t(rowsum(t(rel), group = ifelse(is.na(gen), ".unassigned", gen)))
named     <- setdiff(colnames(by_genus), ".unassigned")
top       <- names(sort(colMeans(by_genus[, named, drop = FALSE]),
                        decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(N_GENERA)]
tidy_gen  <- function(x) sub("_gen_Incertae_sedis", " (unclass.)", x)

GEN_LEVELS <- c(tidy_gen(top), "Other genera", "Unassigned (no genus)")
gen_cat    <- ifelse(is.na(gen), "Unassigned (no genus)",
              ifelse(gen %in% top, tidy_gen(gen), "Other genera"))
gen_share  <- t(rowsum(t(rel), group = gen_cat))[, GEN_LEVELS, drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(all(abs(rowSums(gen_share) - 1) < 1e-10))

# ---- panel B categories: FUNGuild guilds -----------------------------------
# Rule verbatim from 8_functional_guilds.R (itself from 10_hmsc.R), so Figure 1,
# appendix Section 8 and Section 9 classify OTUs identically.
COPRO_GENERA <- c("Sordaria","Podospora","Cercophora","Chaetomium","Schizothecium",
                  "Preussia","Delitschia","Pilobolus","Ascobolus","Saccobolus",
                  "Sporormiella","Coprinopsis","Thelebolus","Coniochaeta")
guild_str <- funguild_otu$Guild[match(colnames(m), funguild_otu$OTU_ID)]
is_copro  <- (!is.na(guild_str) & grepl("Dung Saprotroph", guild_str)) |
             (!is.na(gen)       & gen %in% COPRO_GENERA)
is_plant  <- !is_copro & !is.na(guild_str) &
             grepl("Endophyte|Plant Saprotroph|Plant Pathogen|Epiphyte", guild_str)
is_patho  <- !is_copro & !is_plant & !is.na(guild_str) & grepl("Pathogen|Parasite", guild_str)

GUILD_LEVELS <- c("Dung saprotroph", "Plant-associated", "Pathotroph",
                  "Other assigned", "Unassigned / dark")
guild_cat <- ifelse(is_copro, "Dung saprotroph",
             ifelse(is_plant, "Plant-associated",
             ifelse(is_patho, "Pathotroph",
             ifelse(!is.na(guild_str), "Other assigned", "Unassigned / dark"))))
guild_share <- t(rowsum(t(rel), group = guild_cat))[, GUILD_LEVELS, drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(all(abs(rowSums(guild_share) - 1) < 1e-10))

# ---- shared sample order: descending dung-saprotroph share within season ----
ord <- rownames(rel)[order(Season, -guild_share[, "Dung saprotroph"])]

to_long <- function(mat, levels) data.frame(
  SampleID = factor(rep(rownames(mat), times = ncol(mat)), levels = ord),
  Season   = rep(Season, times = ncol(mat)),
  Category = factor(rep(colnames(mat), each = nrow(mat)), levels = levels),
  share    = as.vector(mat), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
genL <- to_long(gen_share, GEN_LEVELS); guiL <- to_long(guild_share, GUILD_LEVELS)
stopifnot(identical(levels(genL$SampleID), levels(guiL$SampleID)))

# ---- journal style (174 mm double column, 7-8 pt) --------------------------
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(ggtext) })
stopifnot(capabilities("cairo"))          # Unicode glyphs need the cairo devices
FONT  <- "Liberation Sans"                # metric-identical to Arial
PT    <- function(pt) pt / ggplot2::.pt   # pt -> ggplot text size / linewidth (mm)
FIG_W <- 174; FIG_H <- 135                # mm
INK   <- "grey10"
COL_W <- "#0072B2"; COL_S <- "#D55E00"    # winter / summer (repo standard)

theme_journal <- function() {
  theme_classic(base_size = 7, base_family = FONT) +
    theme(text         = element_text(size = 7, colour = INK, family = FONT),
          axis.text    = element_text(size = 7, colour = INK),
          axis.title   = element_text(size = 8, colour = INK),
          axis.line    = element_line(linewidth = PT(0.5), colour = INK),
          axis.ticks   = element_line(linewidth = PT(0.5), colour = INK),
          axis.ticks.length = unit(1, "mm"),
          legend.text  = element_text(size = 7, colour = INK),
          legend.title = element_text(size = 7, colour = INK),
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          strip.text   = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", colour = INK),
          plot.title   = element_blank(),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7, colour = "grey25"),
          plot.tag     = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", colour = "black"),
          plot.margin  = margin(1, 1, 1, 1, "mm"))
}
# Type audit -- fails the build rather than ship text outside 7-8 pt.
audit <- function(p, id) {
  th <- p$theme
  for (nm in c("axis.text.x", "axis.text.y", "axis.title.x", "axis.title.y", "legend.text",
               "legend.title", "strip.text", "plot.subtitle", "plot.tag")) {
    el <- tryCatch(calc_element(nm, th), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(el) || inherits(el, "element_blank") || !is.numeric(el$size)) next
    if (el$size < 7 - 1e-9 || el$size > 8 + 1e-9)
      stop(sprintf("%s: theme %s = %.2f pt (allowed 7-8)", id, nm, el$size))
  }
  for (i in seq_along(p$layers)) {
    l <- p$layers[[i]]
    if (inherits(l$geom, c("GeomText", "GeomLabel", "GeomRichtext", "GeomRichText"))) {
      sz <- l$aes_params$size
      if (is.null(sz)) stop(sprintf("%s: layer %d text has no explicit size", id, i))
      if (sz * ggplot2::.pt < 7 - 1e-9 || sz * ggplot2::.pt > 8 + 1e-9)
        stop(sprintf("%s: layer %d text %.2f pt (allowed 7-8)", id, i, sz * ggplot2::.pt))
    }
    lw <- l$aes_params$linewidth
    if (is.numeric(lw) && lw * ggplot2::.pt < 0.25 - 1e-9)
      stop(sprintf("%s: layer %d linewidth %.2f pt < 0.25", id, i, lw * ggplot2::.pt))
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# ---- colour = guild ---------------------------------------------------------
# One grammar for the whole paper: ORANGE = summer and the dung saprotrophs,
# BLUE = winter and the unassigned / dark taxa. Each genus in panel A is drawn in
# a shade of its guild's hue in panel B, so a column reads the same in both.
UNASS <- "Unassigned (no genus)"
genus_guild <- vapply(setdiff(GEN_LEVELS, c("Other genera", UNASS)), function(g) {
  w <- tapply(colSums(rel[, gen_cat == g, drop = FALSE]), guild_cat[gen_cat == g], sum)
  stopifnot(length(w) == 1L)              # every top genus sits wholly in one guild
  names(w)
}, character(1))
GUILD_COLS <- c("Dung saprotroph" = COL_S, "Plant-associated" = "#3F8F5A",
                "Pathotroph" = "#A8467A", "Other assigned" = "#C7AE74",
                "Unassigned / dark" = COL_W)
SHADES <- list("Dung saprotroph"   = c(COL_S, "#E69F00", "#8C3800", "#F3B37A"),
               "Plant-associated"  = c("#1F6B3F", "#4E9F68", "#9ECC93", "#C9E3BF"),
               "Pathotroph"        = c("#A8467A", "#D58AB0"),
               "Other assigned"    = c("#C7AE74", "#E3D3A8"),
               "Unassigned / dark" = c("#6E9FC9", "#A9C8E4", "#D2E3F1"))
gen_cols <- c()
for (g in names(SHADES)) {
  mem <- names(genus_guild)[genus_guild == g]
  stopifnot(length(mem) <= length(SHADES[[g]]))
  gen_cols <- c(gen_cols, setNames(SHADES[[g]][seq_along(mem)], mem))
}
gen_cols <- c(gen_cols, "Other genera" = "#DCDCDC", setNames(COL_W, UNASS))
# Stack order (bottom -> top) follows the guilds of panel B: dung saprotrophs at
# the base, unassigned / dark on top, so each column's two bars line up.
in_guild <- function(g) names(genus_guild)[genus_guild == g]
GEN_ORDER <- c(unlist(lapply(setdiff(GUILD_LEVELS, "Unassigned / dark"), in_guild)),
               "Other genera", in_guild("Unassigned / dark"), UNASS)
stopifnot(setequal(GEN_ORDER, GEN_LEVELS), setequal(names(gen_cols), GEN_LEVELS))
# Expected membership (2026-11 data); a change here means the palette needs review.
stopifnot(identical(unname(genus_guild[c("Thelebolus", "Sporormiella", "Coniochaeta")]),
                    rep("Dung saprotroph", 3)))

# CVD check on every pair of fill colours that can touch in a column
# (deutan / protan / tritan simulations, CIELAB dE). Reported, and guarded.
cvd_check <- function(cols) {
  sims <- list(normal = cols, deutan = colorspace::deutan(cols),
               protan = colorspace::protan(cols), tritan = colorspace::tritan(cols))
  sapply(sims, function(cc) {
    lab <- grDevices::convertColor(t(grDevices::col2rgb(cc)) / 255, from = "sRGB", to = "Lab")
    min(dist(lab))
  })
}
dE <- cvd_check(unname(gen_cols))
dE_g <- cvd_check(unname(GUILD_COLS))
cat(sprintf("Palette min pairwise dE -- genera: %s | guilds: %s\n",
            paste(sprintf("%s %.1f", names(dE), dE), collapse = ", "),
            paste(sprintf("%s %.1f", names(dE_g), dE_g), collapse = ", ")))
# Floors as for the previous Figure 1 palette (worst CVD dE 7.4 was accepted with
# thin white segment borders as the secondary cue).
stopifnot(min(dE_g) > 10, min(dE) > 6)

# ---- panels A and B: per-dropping bars + one season-mean bar per facet -----
# Continuous x so the mean bar can be set apart: droppings 1..26 at width 1,
# then a gap and a 3-unit "Mean" bar.
MEAN_X <- 26 + 1 + 2; MEAN_W <- 3
xpos <- setNames(ave(seq_along(ord), Season[match(ord, rownames(rel))], FUN = seq_along), ord)
stopifnot(all(table(Season) == 26L))
bars <- function(share, levels) {
  per <- data.frame(SampleID = rep(rownames(share), times = ncol(share)),
                    Season = rep(Season, times = ncol(share)),
                    Category = rep(colnames(share), each = nrow(share)),
                    share = as.vector(share), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  per$x <- xpos[per$SampleID]; per$w <- 1
  mn <- aggregate(share ~ Season + Category, per, mean)
  mn$x <- MEAN_X; mn$w <- MEAN_W; mn$SampleID <- "mean"
  d <- rbind(per[, names(mn)], mn)
  d$Category <- factor(d$Category, levels = levels)
  d <- d[order(d$Season, d$SampleID, d$Category), ]
  d$ymax <- ave(d$share, d$Season, d$SampleID, FUN = cumsum)
  d$ymin <- d$ymax - d$share
  d$Season <- factor(d$Season, levels = c("Winter", "Summer"))
  d
}
genD <- bars(gen_share, GEN_ORDER); guiD <- bars(guild_share, GUILD_LEVELS)

# Guards: per-season means = the committed Section 8 table (guild_season_readshare.csv)
gsr <- read.csv(file.path(if (dir.exists("tables")) "tables" else
                "/home/daniel/Ptarmigan/Scripts_server/Supplementary/tables",
                "guild_season_readshare.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
for (g in GUILD_LEVELS) for (s in c("Winter", "Summer")) {
  ref <- gsr[gsr$Guild == g, if (s == "Winter") "mean_winter" else "mean_summer"]
  got <- guiD$share[guiD$SampleID == "mean" & guiD$Season == s & guiD$Category == g]
  stopifnot(length(got) == 1L, abs(got - ref) < 1e-9)
}
# The season test once drawn as panel C now lives in Figure S-GUILDa(B)
# (Section 8.2). It is recomputed here only as a drift guard: same rule, same
# BH-adjusted Wilcoxon, so the q-values must equal the committed table.
season_stats <- do.call(rbind, lapply(GUILD_LEVELS, function(g) {
  wt <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(guild_share[Season == "Summer", g],
                                     guild_share[Season == "Winter", g]))
  data.frame(Guild = g, p_value = wt$p.value, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
season_stats$q_value <- p.adjust(season_stats$p_value, method = "BH")
stopifnot(max(abs(season_stats$q_value - gsr$q_value[match(GUILD_LEVELS, gsr$Guild)])) < 1e-12)
# Figure 3 draws its bars in this same order from tables/guild_composition_per_sample.csv
# (no RData there); guard that the committed table reproduces it, ties included.
gcs <- read.csv(file.path(if (dir.exists("tables")) "tables" else
                "/home/daniel/Ptarmigan/Scripts_server/Supplementary/tables",
                "guild_composition_per_sample.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
gcs$Season <- factor(gcs$Season, levels = c("Winter", "Summer"))
stopifnot(identical(ord, gcs$SampleID[order(gcs$Season, -gcs[["Dung saprotroph"]])]))
mean_of <- function(d, s, k) 100 * d$share[d$SampleID == "mean" & d$Season == s & d$Category == k]

season_strip <- function(s) sprintf("<span style='color:%s'>**%s**</span> (n = %d droppings)",
                                    c(Winter = COL_W, Summer = COL_S)[s], s, sum(Season == s))
strip_lab <- setNames(vapply(c("Winter", "Summer"), season_strip, ""), c("Winter", "Summer"))

stacked <- function(d, cols, ylab) {
  lab <- d[d$SampleID == "mean" & d$share >= 0.08, ]
  lab$txt <- sprintf("%.0f", 100 * lab$share)
  lum <- grDevices::convertColor(t(grDevices::col2rgb(cols[as.character(lab$Category)])) / 255,
                                 from = "sRGB", to = "Lab")[, 1]
  lab$dark <- lum < 60                                  # white label on dark fills
  ggplot(d) +
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = x - w / 2, xmax = x + w / 2, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = Category),
              colour = "white", linewidth = PT(0.25)) +
    geom_text(data = lab, aes(x = x, y = (ymin + ymax) / 2, label = txt,
                              colour = dark), size = PT(7), family = FONT, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = INK), guide = "none") +
    facet_grid(~ Season, labeller = labeller(Season = strip_lab)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cols, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = MEAN_X, labels = "Mean", expand = c(0, 0.3)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(100 * x, "%"), breaks = c(0, .25, .5, .75, 1),
                       expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = ylab) +
    theme_journal() +
    theme(axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), axis.line.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7, face = "bold", colour = INK,
                                     margin = margin(t = 0.6, unit = "mm")),
          strip.text = element_markdown(size = 8, colour = INK, family = FONT),
          panel.spacing.x = unit(4, "mm"))
}
pA <- stacked(genD, gen_cols, "Genus read share") +
  labs(tag = "A") + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())
pB <- stacked(guiD, GUILD_COLS, "Guild read share") +
  labs(tag = "B") + theme(strip.text = element_blank())

# ---- one key for both panels: guild (B) heads a column of its genera (A) -----
italic_gen <- function(x) ifelse(grepl("unclass\\.|^Other ", x), x, paste0("*", x, "*"))
key_rows <- list()
for (j in seq_along(GUILD_LEVELS)) {
  g <- GUILD_LEVELS[j]
  mem <- intersect(GEN_ORDER, names(genus_guild)[genus_guild == g])
  if (g == "Unassigned / dark") mem <- c(mem, UNASS)
  lab <- if (length(mem)) italic_gen(mem) else character(0)
  lab[mem == UNASS] <- "**No genus: dark taxa**"
  key_rows[[j]] <- rbind(
    data.frame(col = j, row = 0, fill = GUILD_COLS[[g]], txt = sprintf("**%s**", g),
               head = TRUE),
    if (length(mem)) data.frame(col = j, row = seq_along(mem), fill = unname(gen_cols[mem]),
                                txt = lab, head = FALSE))
}
key <- do.call(rbind, key_rows)
key <- rbind(key, data.frame(col = 4, row = 1, fill = gen_cols[["Other genera"]],
                             txt = "Other genera (any guild)", head = FALSE))
KX <- c(0, 0.98, 1.9, 2.55, 3.66)                      # column x positions (0..~4.6)
key$x <- KX[key$col]; key$y <- -key$row
key$y[key$row > 0] <- key$y[key$row > 0] - 0.25       # genera set below their guild
pK <- ggplot(key) +
  # thin rule separating the guild row (panel B) from the genus rows (panel A)
  annotate("segment", x = -0.42, xend = 4.72, y = -0.625, yend = -0.625,
           colour = "grey70", linewidth = PT(0.3)) +
  geom_tile(aes(x = x, y = y, fill = I(fill)), width = 0.075, height = 0.72,
            colour = "white", linewidth = PT(0.25)) +
  geom_richtext(aes(x = x + 0.07, y = y, label = txt), hjust = 0, size = PT(7), family = FONT,
                colour = INK, fill = NA, label.colour = NA, label.padding = unit(0, "mm")) +
  annotate("text", x = -0.06, y = c(0, -1.25), hjust = 1, size = PT(7), family = FONT,
           colour = "grey35", label = c("Guild (B)", "Genus (A)")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.45, 4.75), ylim = c(-3.75, 0.45), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
  theme_void(base_family = FONT) + theme(plot.margin = margin(1, 1, 1, 1, "mm"))

# ---- assemble and write ----------------------------------------------------
for (nm in c("pA", "pB")) audit(get(nm), nm)
fig1 <- pA / pB / free(pK) +
  plot_layout(heights = unit(c(1, 1, 16), c("null", "null", "mm")))

# Every main figure is written three ways: PNG and JPG (600 dpi raster, for
# submission systems that demand one or the other) and PDF (vector, for print).
save_fig <- function(stem, obj, width, height, res = 600) {
  one <- function(open_dev) { open_dev(); on.exit(grDevices::dev.off()); print(obj) }
  png_dev <- if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_png else grDevices::png
  one(function() png_dev(paste0(stem, ".png"), width = width, height = height,
                         units = "in", res = res))
  one(function() grDevices::jpeg(paste0(stem, ".jpg"), width = width, height = height,
                                 units = "in", res = res, quality = 95))
  one(function() grDevices::cairo_pdf(paste0(stem, ".pdf"), width = width, height = height))
}
save_fig(file.path(out_dir, "Fig1_composition_function"), fig1, FIG_W / 25.4, FIG_H / 25.4)

cat(sprintf("Top %d genera (mean per-sample read share, %%):\n", N_GENERA))
print(round(100 * colMeans(gen_share), 2))
cat("Genus -> guild:\n"); print(genus_guild)
```

### 10.2 Figure 2 — Seasonal niche across OTUs, lineages and guilds (HMSC)

:::: {.content-visible when-profile="docs"}
*Provenance: all three panels read committed tables of Section 9 (headline abundance model): Fig. 2A `tables/hmsc_beta_season.csv` (Section 9.4; the 22 most abundant OTUs with intervals are Figure S-HMSCg), Fig. 2B Tables S-HMSCf3 and S-HMSCf4 and `tables/hmsc_rho_phylo.csv` (Section 9.6), Fig. 2C Tables S-HMSCc and S-HMSCc2 (Section 9.2). The former main-text Figure 2 (H1 ordination and centroid distance) is now Figures S6 and S6b of Section 4.*
::::

![](figures/main/Fig2_hmsc_season_niche.png)

**Figure 2**: Seasonal niche of the dung mycobiome across OTUs, lineages and guilds. All panels come from one abundance (CLR) HMSC model of 226 OTUs in 55 droppings, with each dropping's two PCR replicates averaged, Season and Year as fixed effects and the dropping as random level. **(A)** Posterior mean Season coefficient of every OTU (positive = more abundant in summer). Coloured points have a 95% credible interval excluding zero (44 winter-shifted, 30 summer-shifted); grey points do not. Below: mean (triangle) and interquartile range of the per-OTU coefficients within each guild. **(B)** Percentage of OTUs in each fungal class with a positive Season coefficient (filled points; Table S-HMSCf3), and the same after adding each dropping's log library depth as a covariate (open points; Table S-HMSCf4); brackets give the phylum values. Stars give a permutation test of the class's mean standardised coefficient against random groups of the same size (\* p \< 0.05, \*\* p \< 0.01, \*\*\* p \< 0.001). The box gives the phylogenetic signal ρ of the Season responses, with 95% credible interval, from the HMSC phylogeny variant (Appendix Section 9.6). **(C)** Mean share of per-OTU explained variance attributed to Season, Year and the dropping, for all OTUs, dung saprotrophs and unassigned / dark OTUs; *Season + Year* is the fixed-effect total. The italic column (*) is the share of total CLR variance lying between the two PCR replicates of a dropping, estimated outside the model (Table S-HMSCc2). Guilds are the model's five-level trait, which places 46 OTUs with a genus but no FUNGuild call in *Other assigned* rather than *Unassigned / dark* as in Figure 1 (Appendix Section 8.1).

:::: {.content-visible when-profile="docs"}
*Narrative carried over from the former Figure 3, whose panel A is now Figure S-HMSCg and whose panel B is panel C here; to be rewritten for the new figure.*

Panel A makes the seasonal signal concrete at the level of individual lineages, and it does so among the taxa that actually constitute the community: the 22 OTUs plotted are every OTU holding at least 1% of modelled read share, and they carry 73% of the modelled reads between them.
Read from the top, the panel is the study's taxonomic result in one column. The summer end is an unbroken block of coprophilous dung saprotrophs — *Thelebolus* (OTU1, β = +4.17), *Sporormiella* (OTU636, +3.52), *Coniochaeta* (OTU1225, +3.44) and two further Sporormiaceae and Coniochaetaceae lineages — every one of them resolved. The winter end is a block dominated by dark, taxonomically unresolved taxa, ending at OTU1369 (−5.00), the unclassified Dothideomycete that dominates winter read share in Figure 3. Plant-associated taxa straddle zero between them. The guild means below make the same statement over all 226 OTUs rather than the 22 shown. Dung saprotrophs (+1.32) have by far the most summer-shifted mean; dark/unassigned taxa (−0.31) and pathotrophs (−0.33) lean winter; and the yeast-rich "other" group is weakly positive (+0.22). The model's trait-level estimate agrees: the dung-saprotroph guild's Season effect is positive with posterior support 0.994, and dark/unassigned, pathotroph and plant-associated OTUs respond clearly less summer-ward (Section 9.3). Panel B sizes these effects. Season accounts for 31.5% of the variance the model explains and Year for 18.5%, while half (49.9%) sits among droppings — one dropping to the next. The Season share is largest for dung saprotrophs (49.8%): coprophiles are the taxa whose abundance season determines most. Measured separately, a further 32% of total CLR variance is replicate-to-replicate noise within a dropping, most of it whether rare taxa are detected at all; coprophiles are the most repeatable guild (17%). Taken together the panels state the central quantitative claim in one place: seasonal turnover is real, directional and consistent across methods, yet it sits beside large idiosyncrasy among individual droppings — which is why the model explains the samples it has seen (R² ≈ 0.29) but predicts held-out droppings far less well (cross-validated R² ≈ 0.03; Section 9.7).
::::

```{r fig2-build}
#| eval: false
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()

# Figure 2 -- Seasonal niche across lineages (HMSC, H1 synthesis).
# Journal layout: 174 mm double column, 7-8 pt text (FEMS Microbiology Ecology).
# Every number is READ from committed tables/ CSVs written by 10_hmsc.R; no model
# is loaded or refitted here.
#   A  tables/hmsc_beta_season.csv               per-OTU Season beta (CLR), all 226 OTUs
#   B  tables/hmsc_season_by_lineage.csv          Table S-HMSCf3 (share summer-positive)
#      tables/hmsc_season_by_lineage_depth.csv    Table S-HMSCf4 (same, read depth controlled)
#      tables/hmsc_rho_phylo.csv                  phylogenetic signal rho (Section 9.6)
#   C  tables/hmsc_variance_partition.csv         per-OTU variance components (CLR)
#      tables/hmsc_pcr_replicate_variance.csv     model-free PCR-replicate share
# All panels use the headline ABUNDANCE (CLR) model: CLR averaged over each
# dropping's two PCR replicates, dropping as random level (Section 9.1).
# Colour grammar shared with Figure 1: ORANGE = summer and the coprophilous dung
# saprotrophs, BLUE = winter and the unassigned / dark taxa, greys = the rest.
# Rebuild:  conda run -n r_env Rscript build_main_figure.R fig2-build

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2); library(patchwork); library(ggtext)
})
stopifnot(capabilities("cairo"))          # Unicode glyphs (beta, rho, arrows) need cairo

tab_dir <- if (dir.exists("tables")) "tables" else
           "/home/daniel/Ptarmigan/Scripts_server/Supplementary/tables"
out_dir <- "figures/main"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
grDevices::pdf(NULL)                                  # headless: no X11 fallback

# ---- journal style ---------------------------------------------------------
FONT  <- "Liberation Sans"                # metric-identical to Arial
PT    <- function(pt) pt / ggplot2::.pt   # pt -> ggplot text size / linewidth (mm)
FIG_W <- 174; FIG_H <- 155                # mm
COL_W <- "#0072B2"; COL_S <- "#D55E00"    # winter / summer (repo standard)
COL_RES <- "#5A5A5A"; COL_UNRES <- "#D4D4D4"; INK <- "grey10"

theme_journal <- function() {
  theme_classic(base_size = 7, base_family = FONT) +
    theme(text         = element_text(size = 7, colour = INK, family = FONT),
          axis.text    = element_text(size = 7, colour = INK),
          axis.title   = element_text(size = 8, colour = INK),
          axis.line    = element_line(linewidth = PT(0.5), colour = INK),
          axis.ticks   = element_line(linewidth = PT(0.5), colour = INK),
          axis.ticks.length = unit(1, "mm"),
          legend.text  = element_text(size = 7, colour = INK),
          legend.title = element_text(size = 7, colour = INK),
          legend.key.size = unit(3, "mm"),
          legend.background = element_blank(),
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          strip.text   = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", colour = INK),
          plot.title   = element_blank(),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7, colour = "grey25", margin = margin(b = 1, unit = "mm")),
          plot.tag     = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", colour = "black"),
          plot.margin  = margin(1, 1, 1, 1, "mm"))
}

# Type audit -- fails the build rather than ship text outside 7-8 pt.
audit <- function(p, id) {
  th <- p$theme
  for (nm in c("axis.text.x", "axis.text.y", "axis.title.x", "axis.title.y", "legend.text",
               "legend.title", "strip.text", "plot.subtitle", "plot.tag")) {
    el <- tryCatch(calc_element(nm, th), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(el) || inherits(el, "element_blank") || !is.numeric(el$size)) next
    if (el$size < 7 - 1e-9 || el$size > 8 + 1e-9)
      stop(sprintf("%s: theme %s = %.2f pt (allowed 7-8)", id, nm, el$size))
  }
  for (i in seq_along(p$layers)) {
    l <- p$layers[[i]]
    if (inherits(l$geom, c("GeomText", "GeomLabel", "GeomRichtext", "GeomRichText"))) {
      sz <- l$aes_params$size
      if (is.null(sz)) stop(sprintf("%s: layer %d text has no explicit size", id, i))
      if (sz * ggplot2::.pt < 7 - 1e-9 || sz * ggplot2::.pt > 8 + 1e-9)
        stop(sprintf("%s: layer %d text %.2f pt (allowed 7-8)", id, i, sz * ggplot2::.pt))
    }
    lw <- l$aes_params$linewidth
    if (is.numeric(lw) && lw * ggplot2::.pt < 0.25 - 1e-9)
      stop(sprintf("%s: layer %d linewidth %.2f pt < 0.25", id, i, lw * ggplot2::.pt))
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# Measured panel body (mm) of a ggplot drawn at w x h mm -- used to lay the
# beeswarm out in printed millimetres.
panel_mm <- function(p, w_mm, h_mm) {
  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf")
  grDevices::cairo_pdf(f, width = w_mm / 25.4, height = h_mm / 25.4)
  on.exit({ grDevices::dev.off(); unlink(f) }, add = TRUE)
  grid::grid.newpage()
  grid::grid.draw(if (inherits(p, "patchwork")) patchwork::patchworkGrob(p) else ggplotGrob(p))
  grid::grid.force()
  vp <- grid::grid.ls(viewports = TRUE, grobs = FALSE, print = FALSE)$name
  vp <- unique(vp[grepl("^panel", vp)])
  vapply(vp, function(v) {
    grid::seekViewport(v)
    c(w = grid::convertWidth(unit(1, "npc"), "mm", valueOnly = TRUE),
      h = grid::convertHeight(unit(1, "npc"), "mm", valueOnly = TRUE))
  }, numeric(2))
}

guild_map <- c(dung_saprotroph = "Dung saprotroph", plant_associated = "Plant-associated",
               pathotroph = "Pathotroph", other = "Other assigned",
               dark_unassigned = "Unassigned / dark")

# ============================================================================
# Panel A -- Season effect of all 226 modelled OTUs as one beeswarm
# ============================================================================
b <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "hmsc_beta_season.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
b$beta <- b$beta_season_mean
b$res  <- b$beta_season_CrI2.5 > 0 | b$beta_season_CrI97.5 < 0      # 95% CrI excludes 0
stopifnot(nrow(b) == 226L, !anyNA(b$beta), setequal(b$guild, names(guild_map)),
          sum(b$res) == 74L, sum(b$res & b$beta < 0) == 44L, sum(b$res & b$beta > 0) == 30L)
b$Guild <- factor(unname(guild_map[b$guild]), levels = guild_map)

# Drift guards: the four labelled OTUs (Section 9.4) and the guild means (Section 9.3).
flag <- c(OTU1 = 4.166, OTU636 = 3.515, OTU1225 = 3.443, OTU1369 = -5.004)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(b$beta[match(names(flag), b$OTU_ID)], unname(flag))),
          identical(b$Genus[match(c("OTU1", "OTU636", "OTU1225"), b$OTU_ID)],
                    c("Thelebolus", "Sporormiella", "Coniochaeta")),
          is.na(b$Genus[b$OTU_ID == "OTU1369"]), all(b$res[match(names(flag), b$OTU_ID)]))
gm <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(b$Guild), function(g) {
  x <- b$beta[b$Guild == g]
  data.frame(Guild = g, n = length(x), mean = mean(x),
             q1 = unname(quantile(x, 0.25)), q3 = unname(quantile(x, 0.75)))
}))
stopifnot(identical(round(gm$mean, 2), c(1.32, -0.10, -0.33, 0.22, -0.31)),
          identical(gm$n, c(14L, 50L, 16L, 67L, 79L)))

b$cls <- factor(ifelse(!b$res, "Not resolved (95% CrI spans 0)",
                ifelse(b$guild == "dung_saprotroph", "Dung saprotroph",
                ifelse(b$guild == "dark_unassigned", "Unassigned / dark", "Other guilds"))),
                levels = c("Dung saprotroph", "Unassigned / dark", "Other guilds",
                           "Not resolved (95% CrI spans 0)"))
FILLS <- setNames(c(COL_S, COL_W, COL_RES, COL_UNRES), levels(b$cls))
GM_COL <- c("Dung saprotroph" = COL_S, "Plant-associated" = COL_RES, "Pathotroph" = COL_RES,
            "Other assigned" = COL_RES, "Unassigned / dark" = COL_W)

# Beeswarm laid out in printed millimetres, so circles of diameter D_MM never
# overlap at the final size: x is converted with the MEASURED panel width.
# Panel A's BODY height is set to exactly the y range it needs and fixed in the
# layout, so that 1 y unit = 1 printed mm (circles stay round and never overlap).
XLIM  <- c(-5.6, 5.4)
D_MM  <- 1.20                                 # centre-to-centre spacing (mm)
PT_SZ <- 1.08 / 0.75                          # shape 21: diameter ~ 0.75 * size mm
swarm <- function(x_mm, D) {
  o <- order(abs(x_mm - median(x_mm)))        # densest first -> compact centre
  y <- rep(NA_real_, length(x_mm))
  for (i in o) {
    placed <- which(!is.na(y))
    near   <- placed[abs(x_mm[placed] - x_mm[i]) < D]
    if (!length(near)) { y[i] <- 0; next }
    h  <- sqrt(D^2 - (x_mm[near] - x_mm[i])^2)
    lo <- y[near] - h; hi <- y[near] + h
    cand <- c(0, lo, hi)
    ok <- vapply(cand, function(c) all(c <= lo + 1e-9 | c >= hi - 1e-9), logical(1))
    cand <- cand[ok]
    y[i] <- cand[which.min(abs(cand))]
  }
  y
}

build_A <- function(panel_w_mm) {
  mm_per_x <- panel_w_mm / diff(XLIM)
  b$y <- swarm(b$beta * mm_per_x, D_MM)
  ytop <- max(b$y); ybot <- min(b$y)
  # guild-mean block: one row per guild below the swarm (mean = triangle,
  # interquartile range of per-OTU posterior means = bar)
  ROW_GAP <- 2.9
  gm_ord <- c("Dung saprotroph", "Other assigned", "Plant-associated",
              "Unassigned / dark", "Pathotroph")         # by mean, summer -> winter
  g2 <- gm[match(gm_ord, gm$Guild), ]
  g2$y <- ybot - 6.4 - (seq_len(nrow(g2)) - 1) * ROW_GAP
  g2$col <- GM_COL[g2$Guild]
  g2$lab <- sprintf("%s (n = %d)", g2$Guild, g2$n)
  g2$val <- sub("-", "−", sprintf("%+.2f", g2$mean))
  y_sep <- ybot - 2.2
  y_hi <- ytop + 2.5; y_lo <- min(g2$y) - 1.6

  pos <- function(id) b[b$OTU_ID == id, c("beta", "y")]
  th <- pos("OTU1"); sp <- pos("OTU636"); co <- pos("OTU1225"); dk <- pos("OTU1369")
  r <- D_MM / 2
  # Sporormiella and Coniochaeta sit 0.07 apart: the higher one is labelled
  # above, the other below, so no leader crosses a point.
  up <- if (co$y >= sp$y) "co" else "sp"
  pu <- if (up == "co") co else sp; pd <- if (up == "co") sp else co
  LIFT <- 4.2
  lab <- data.frame(
    x  = c(th$beta + 0.13, pu$beta - 0.18, pd$beta + 0.18, dk$beta - 0.07),
    y  = c(th$y, pu$y + LIFT, pd$y - LIFT, dk$y + 2.6),
    hj = c(0, 1, 0, 0), vj = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0),
    col = c(COL_S, COL_S, COL_S, COL_W),
    txt = c("*Thelebolus*",
            if (up == "co") "*Coniochaeta*" else "*Sporormiella*",
            if (up == "co") "*Sporormiella*" else "*Coniochaeta*",
            "**OTU1369**<br>undescribed Dothideomycetes"))
  seg <- data.frame(x = c(pu$beta, pd$beta, dk$beta), y = c(pu$y + r, pd$y - r, dk$y + r),
                    xend = c(pu$beta - 0.15, pd$beta + 0.15, dk$beta),
                    yend = c(pu$y + LIFT, pd$y - LIFT, dk$y + 2.4))

  p <- ggplot(b, aes(beta, y)) +
    annotate("segment", x = 0, xend = 0, y = y_sep, yend = ytop + 2,
             colour = "grey55", linewidth = PT(0.5), linetype = "22") +
    annotate("segment", x = XLIM[1], xend = XLIM[2], y = y_sep, yend = y_sep,
             colour = "grey80", linewidth = PT(0.4)) +
    geom_segment(data = seg, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
                 inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey35", linewidth = PT(0.5)) +
    geom_point(aes(fill = cls), shape = 21, size = PT_SZ, colour = "white", stroke = 0.25) +
    # guild-mean block
    geom_segment(data = g2, aes(x = q1, xend = q3, y = y, yend = y), inherit.aes = FALSE,
                 colour = g2$col, linewidth = PT(1.6), alpha = 0.55, lineend = "butt") +
    geom_point(data = g2, aes(mean, y), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 24, fill = g2$col,
               colour = "white", size = 2.2, stroke = 0.3) +
    geom_text(data = g2, aes(x = XLIM[1] + 0.05, y = y, label = lab), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              hjust = 0, size = PT(7), colour = g2$col, family = FONT,
              fontface = ifelse(g2$col == COL_RES, "plain", "bold")) +
    geom_text(data = g2, aes(x = pmax(q3, mean) + 0.12, y = y, label = val), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              hjust = 0, size = PT(7), colour = g2$col, family = FONT) +
    annotate("text", x = XLIM[1] + 0.05, y = g2$y[1] + ROW_GAP * 0.92, hjust = 0,
             label = "Guild mean (▲) and interquartile range",
             size = PT(7), colour = "grey30", family = FONT, fontface = "italic") +
    geom_richtext(data = lab, aes(x = x, y = y, label = txt, hjust = hj, vjust = vj),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = lab$col, size = PT(7.5), family = FONT,
                  fill = NA, label.colour = NA, label.padding = unit(0, "mm"),
                  lineheight = 1.1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = FILLS, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = -5:5, labels = function(v) sub("-", "−", v)) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = XLIM, ylim = c(y_lo, y_hi),
                    expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
    labs(y = NULL, x = sprintf(paste0(
      "Season effect (HMSC β, CLR abundance) of each of the 226 modelled OTUs<br>",
      "<span style='color:%s'>**← more abundant in winter: 44 resolved**</span>",
      "&#8195;&#8195;",
      "<span style='color:%s'>**more abundant in summer: 30 resolved →**</span>"),
      COL_W, COL_S)) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1, override.aes = list(size = 1.9))) +
    theme_journal() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          axis.line.y = element_blank(),
          axis.title.x = element_markdown(size = 8, colour = INK, lineheight = 1.25,
                                          margin = margin(t = 1.2, unit = "mm"), family = FONT),
          legend.position = "bottom", legend.justification = "centre",
          legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0), legend.box.spacing = unit(1.5, "mm"),
          legend.key.spacing.x = unit(2.5, "mm"),
          plot.margin = margin(1, 4, 1, 1, "mm"))
  attr(p, "body_h_mm") <- y_hi - y_lo
  p
}

# ============================================================================
# Panel B -- share of summer-positive OTUs by class (taxonomy, no tree)
# ============================================================================
ln <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "hmsc_season_by_lineage.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
dp <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "hmsc_season_by_lineage_depth.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
rho <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "hmsc_rho_phylo.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(ln) == 11L, sum(ln$rank == "Class") == 9L,
          identical(paste(ln$rank, ln$lineage), paste(dp$rank, dp$lineage)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(ln$pct_summer_positive, dp$pct_pos_hmsc)),
          abs(ln$pct_summer_positive[ln$lineage == "Basidiomycota"] - 71.8) < 0.05,
          abs(ln$pct_summer_positive[ln$lineage == "Ascomycota"] - 43.1) < 0.05,
          # Section 9.6 / Table S-HMSCf4 numbers
          abs(dp$pct_pos_lm_logdepth[dp$lineage == "Basidiomycota"] - 83.33) < 0.01,
          abs(dp$pct_pos_lm_logdepth[dp$lineage == "Ascomycota"] - 54.17) < 0.01,
          nrow(rho) == 1L, rho$param == "rho", rho$median == 0.99, rho$psrf < 1.01)
ln$depth <- dp$pct_pos_lm_logdepth
star <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "***", ifelse(p < 0.01, "**", ifelse(p < 0.05, "*", "")))

BASIDIO <- c("Microbotryomycetes", "Tremellomycetes", "Agaricomycetes")
cls <- ln[ln$rank == "Class", ]
cls$grp <- factor(ifelse(cls$lineage %in% BASIDIO, "Basidiomycota",
                  ifelse(cls$lineage == "unassigned", "unassigned", "Ascomycota")),
                  levels = c("Basidiomycota", "Ascomycota", "unassigned"))
cls <- cls[order(cls$grp, -cls$pct_summer_positive), ]
cls$name <- ifelse(cls$lineage == "unassigned", "No class assigned", cls$lineage)
GAP <- 0.6
cls$y <- -(seq_len(nrow(cls)) + (as.integer(cls$grp) - 1) * GAP)
cls$dir  <- ifelse(cls$pct_summer_positive >= 50, "Summer", "Winter")
cls$star <- star(cls$p_perm)
cls$lab  <- sprintf("%s <span style='color:#808080'>(%d)</span>%s", cls$name, cls$n_otu,
                    ifelse(cls$star == "", "", paste0(" ", cls$star)))

ph <- ln[ln$rank == "Phylum", ]
ph <- data.frame(grp = ph$lineage, pct = ph$pct_summer_positive, depth = ph$depth,
                 n = ph$n_otu, star = star(ph$p_perm))
ph$ytop <- sapply(ph$grp, function(g) max(cls$y[cls$grp == g])) + 0.4
ph$ybot <- sapply(ph$grp, function(g) min(cls$y[cls$grp == g])) - 0.4
ph$col  <- ifelse(ph$pct >= 50, COL_S, COL_W)
ph$txt  <- sprintf("**%s**<br>%d%% of %d %s<br><span style='color:#606060'>%d%% depth-adj.</span>",
                   ph$grp, round(ph$pct), ph$n, ph$star, round(ph$depth))
XB <- 104

rho_txt <- sprintf("**Phylogenetic signal**<br>ρ = %.2f<br>95%% CrI %.3f–%.3f",
                   rho$median, rho$CrI_2.5, rho$CrI_97.5)

pB <- ggplot(cls, aes(y = y)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 50, colour = "grey40", linewidth = PT(0.5)) +
  geom_segment(data = ph, aes(x = pct, xend = pct, y = ytop, yend = ybot), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               colour = ph$col, linewidth = PT(0.6), linetype = "22") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 50, xend = pct_summer_positive, yend = y, colour = dir),
               linewidth = PT(2.2)) +
  geom_point(aes(x = pct_summer_positive, colour = dir), size = 2.3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = depth), shape = 21, fill = "white", colour = "grey20",
             size = 1.5, stroke = 0.45) +
  geom_segment(data = ph, aes(x = XB, xend = XB, y = ytop, yend = ybot), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               colour = ph$col, linewidth = PT(0.6)) +
  geom_segment(data = rbind(transform(ph, yy = ytop), transform(ph, yy = ybot)),
               aes(x = XB - 1.5, xend = XB, y = yy, yend = yy), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               colour = c(ph$col, ph$col), linewidth = PT(0.6)) +
  geom_richtext(data = ph, aes(x = XB + 2.5, y = (ytop + ybot) / 2, label = txt),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, colour = ph$col, size = PT(7),
                family = FONT, lineheight = 1.15, fill = NA, label.colour = NA,
                label.padding = unit(0, "mm")) +
  # phylogenetic signal of the same Season responses (Section 9.6), in the
  # margin directly under the Ascomycota bracket
  annotate("richtext", x = XB + 1.5, y = ph$ybot[ph$grp == "Ascomycota"] - 0.15, label = rho_txt,
           hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = PT(7), family = FONT, colour = INK, lineheight = 1.2,
           fill = "grey95", label.colour = NA, label.padding = unit(c(0.7, 1, 0.7, 1), "mm"),
           label.r = unit(0.6, "mm")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Winter = COL_W, Summer = COL_S), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = cls$y, labels = cls$lab, expand = expansion(add = 0.55)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
                     expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-2, 102), clip = "off") +
  labs(y = NULL, subtitle = paste0(
         "<span style='color:#404040'>● HMSC model&#8195;○ read depth controlled ",
         "(log library size)</span>"),
       x = sprintf(paste0("OTUs more abundant in summer (β > 0)<br>",
                          "<span style='color:%s'>**← leans winter**</span>&#8195;",
                          "<span style='color:%s'>**leans summer →**</span>"), COL_W, COL_S)) +
  theme_journal() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_markdown(size = 7, colour = INK, family = FONT),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        plot.subtitle = element_markdown(size = 7, colour = INK, lineheight = 1.3,
                                         family = FONT, margin = margin(b = 1.5, unit = "mm")),
        axis.title.x = element_markdown(size = 8, colour = INK, lineheight = 1.25, family = FONT,
                                        margin = margin(t = 1.2, unit = "mm")),
        plot.margin = margin(1, 25, 1, 1, "mm"))

# ============================================================================
# Panel C -- variance partition, community + the two story guilds
# ============================================================================
vp <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "hmsc_variance_partition.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
VP_LEVELS <- c("Season", "Year", "Random: sample")
stopifnot(nrow(vp) == 226L, setequal(vp$OTU_ID, b$OTU_ID),
          max(abs(rowSums(vp[, VP_LEVELS]) - 1)) < 1e-3)        # stored at 4 dp
vp$Guild <- unname(guild_map[vp$guild])
ROWS <- c("All modelled OTUs", "Dung saprotroph", "Unassigned / dark")
vpm <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ROWS, function(g) {
  d <- if (g == ROWS[1]) vp else vp[vp$Guild == g, ]
  data.frame(grp = g, n = nrow(d), t(colMeans(d[, VP_LEVELS])), check.names = FALSE)
}))
stopifnot(identical(vpm$n, c(226L, 14L, 79L)),
          max(abs(100 * vpm$Season - c(31.53, 49.8, 33.1))) < 0.06,
          abs(100 * vpm$Year[1] - 18.55) < 0.05)
pcr <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "hmsc_pcr_replicate_variance.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
vpm$pcr <- pcr$share_total_mean[match(c("all", "dung_saprotroph", "dark_unassigned"), pcr$group)]
stopifnot(!anyNA(vpm$pcr), identical(round(100 * vpm$pcr), c(32, 17, 34)))

VP_COLS <- c("Season" = "#3E3A78", "Year" = "#A29CCB", "Dropping" = "#BDBDBD")
# Row labels sit ABOVE each bar (not on a y axis) so the bars get the width.
vpm$y <- c(3.2, 1.75, 0.55)                              # community row set apart
H <- 0.6
rect <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(vpm)), function(i) {
  v <- 100 * unlist(vpm[i, VP_LEVELS], use.names = FALSE)
  data.frame(comp = factor(names(VP_COLS), levels = names(VP_COLS)),
             xmin = c(0, cumsum(v)[-3]), xmax = cumsum(v), ymin = vpm$y[i] - H / 2,
             ymax = vpm$y[i] + H / 2)
}))
vpm$col <- c(INK, COL_S, COL_W)
vpm$lab <- sprintf("<span style='color:%s'>**%s**</span> <span style='color:#606060'>(n = %d)</span>",
                   vpm$col, vpm$grp, vpm$n)
X_TOT <- 111; X_PCR <- 140; X_DIV <- 125.5
hdr_y <- max(vpm$y) + H / 2 + 0.55

pC <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = rect, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = comp),
            colour = "white", linewidth = PT(0.4)) +
  geom_richtext(data = vpm, aes(x = 0, y = y + H / 2 + 0.06, label = lab), hjust = 0,
                vjust = 0, size = PT(7), family = FONT, fill = NA, label.colour = NA,
                label.padding = unit(0, "mm")) +
  geom_text(data = vpm, aes(x = 100 * Season / 2, y = y, label = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * Season)),
            colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = PT(7), family = FONT) +
  geom_text(data = vpm, aes(x = X_TOT, y = y, label = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (Season + Year))),
            colour = INK, size = PT(7), family = FONT) +
  geom_text(data = vpm, aes(x = X_PCR, y = y, label = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * pcr)),
            colour = INK, size = PT(7), family = FONT, fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = c(X_TOT, X_PCR), y = hdr_y, vjust = 0, lineheight = 0.95,
           label = c("Season\n+ Year", "PCR\nreplicate*"), size = PT(7), family = FONT,
           colour = "grey30", fontface = c("plain", "italic")) +
  annotate("segment", x = X_DIV, xend = X_DIV, y = min(vpm$y) - H / 2, yend = hdr_y + 1.1,
           colour = "grey60", linewidth = PT(0.4), linetype = "22") +
  annotate("segment", x = 0, xend = X_PCR + 6, y = vpm$y[1] - H / 2 - 0.38,
           yend = vpm$y[1] - H / 2 - 0.38, colour = "grey80", linewidth = PT(0.4)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = VP_COLS, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
                     expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(min(vpm$y) - H / 2 - 0.15, hdr_y + 1.15),
                  clip = "off") +
  labs(x = "Share of explained variance", y = NULL) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) +
  theme_journal() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.line.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
        legend.box.spacing = unit(1, "mm"), legend.key.spacing.x = unit(2, "mm"),
        plot.margin = margin(1, 21, 1, 3, "mm"))

# ---- assemble and write ----------------------------------------------------
# The bottom row is wrapped as one element, so panel A is NOT aligned with it
# (B's long class labels would otherwise squeeze the swarm) and A's body height
# can be fixed in mm. Tags are therefore set by hand. A thin rule (its own 3 mm
# row) separates panel A, legend included, from panels B and C.
rule <- wrap_elements(full = grid::linesGrob(x = unit(c(0.01, 0.99), "npc"), y = unit(0.5, "npc"),
                                             gp = grid::gpar(col = "grey70", lwd = 0.6)))
assemble <- function(pA) (pA + labs(tag = "A")) / rule /
  wrap_elements(full = (pB + labs(tag = "B")) + (pC + labs(tag = "C")) +
                  plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1.05))) +
  plot_layout(heights = unit(c(attr(pA, "body_h_mm"), 3, 1), c("mm", "mm", "null")))
a_dims <- function(pA) {                      # A's body inside the assembled figure
  d <- panel_mm(assemble(pA), FIG_W, FIG_H)
  d[, which.min(abs(d["h", ] - attr(pA, "body_h_mm")) + abs(d["w", ] - max(d["w", ]))),
    drop = TRUE]
}
# Measure panel A's printed width, rebuild the swarm against it, until stable.
pw <- FIG_W - 8
for (k in 1:4) {
  pA <- build_A(pw)
  pw_new <- a_dims(pA)[["w"]]
  if (abs(pw_new - pw) < 0.05) break
  pw <- pw_new
}
pA <- build_A(pw)
ad <- a_dims(pA)                              # guard: 1 y unit = 1 printed mm
stopifnot(abs(ad[["w"]] - pw) < 0.1, abs(ad[["h"]] - attr(pA, "body_h_mm")) < 0.1)
for (nm in c("pA", "pB", "pC")) audit(get(nm), nm)
fig2 <- assemble(pA)

# Every main figure is written three ways: PNG and JPG (600 dpi raster, for
# submission systems that demand one or the other) and PDF (vector, for print).
save_fig <- function(stem, obj, width, height, res = 600) {
  one <- function(open_dev) { open_dev(); on.exit(grDevices::dev.off()); print(obj) }
  png_dev <- if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_png else grDevices::png
  one(function() png_dev(paste0(stem, ".png"), width = width, height = height,
                         units = "in", res = res))
  one(function() grDevices::jpeg(paste0(stem, ".jpg"), width = width, height = height,
                                 units = "in", res = res, quality = 95))
  one(function() grDevices::cairo_pdf(paste0(stem, ".pdf"), width = width, height = height))
}
save_fig(file.path(out_dir, "Fig2_hmsc_season_niche"), fig2, FIG_W / 25.4, FIG_H / 25.4)

cat(sprintf("Panel A body %.1f mm wide; %d OTUs, %d resolved (%d winter / %d summer)\n",
            pw, nrow(b), sum(b$res), sum(b$res & b$beta < 0), sum(b$res & b$beta > 0)))
print(data.frame(gm[, 1:2], mean = round(gm$mean, 2)), row.names = FALSE)
print(data.frame(group = vpm$grp, n = vpm$n, round(100 * vpm[, VP_LEVELS], 1),
                 pcr = round(100 * vpm$pcr), check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

### 10.3 Figure 3 — Dark, largely novel lineages dominate winter dung (E1)

:::: {.content-visible when-profile="docs"}
*Provenance: both panels come from Section 3.4. Fig. 3A is built from `tables/E1_SH_readshare_by_sample.csv`, written by `9_dark_taxa_SH_matching.R` Section 4b, in Figure 1's sample order (read from `tables/guild_composition_per_sample.csv`; fig1-build asserts the two orders agree); its mean bars are the former Fig. 5B. Fig. 3B plots Table S-E1b (the former Fig. 5C). The OTU counts in the key are those of Figure S-E1b (the former Fig. 5A), with the last two categories merged. Every value is read from committed `tables/` CSVs; nothing is recomputed from sequence data, because the Species Hypothesis assignment is an external pipeline step.*
::::

![](figures/main/Fig3_dark_taxa_SH.png)

**Figure 3**: Winter dung is dominated by fungal lineages missing from reference databases. **(A)** Per-dropping read share of OTUs with a genus assignment (grey) and of dark OTUs, those with no confident genus, split by their placement against UNITE Species Hypotheses (SH): inside an existing named SH, forming a candidate new SH, or with no UNITE relative within 80% identity (this last category also holds 13 OTUs removed by quality control before matching). Droppings are in the order of Figure 1, and the right-hand bar of each season is the mean over its droppings, labelled in % for segments of at least 5%. The subtitle gives the Wilcoxon rank-sum test of the candidate-new-SH share between seasons, and the key the number of OTUs in each category. **(B)** The 30 dark OTUs with the highest mean winter read share (Table S-E1b): the number of winter droppings in which each was detected against its mean read share per winter dropping (filled points), joined to the same OTU's mean share per summer dropping (open points). The most abundant, OTU1369, is labelled with its finest resolved rank and its identity to the nearest UNITE reference.

:::: {.content-visible when-profile="docs"}
*Narrative carried over from the former Figure 5 (A = OTU counts per placement, now Figure S-E1b and the key; B = season means, now the mean bars of panel A; C = panel B); to be rewritten for the new figure.*

**Former Figure 5 legend (full version)**: Winter dung is dominated by fungal lineages that carry no confident genus, and most of that fraction is not merely unnamed but absent from the reference database. **(A)** UNITE Species Hypothesis placement of all 493 dark OTUs — those the naïve-Bayes classifier leaves without a confident genus. The second and third categories are the same kind of outcome: neither falls inside an existing named Species Hypothesis, and they differ only in whether the sequence has any UNITE relative at all. "Candidate novel SH" has one (median best hit 92.0% identity across these 228 OTUs) and so inherits a partial lineage from its neighbours; "no reference within 80% id" has none, and additionally absorbs 13 OTUs that the pipeline filtered before the matching step. Together they are 331 of the 493 dark OTUs (67%). **(B)** Mean per-sample read share of the same categories, by season, with the named fraction added to reach 100% of reads (52 droppings, 26 per season; segments below 5% are unlabelled). This is the read-weighted counterpart to (A): counting OTUs says nothing about how much of a dropping they are. Candidate-novel lineages hold 29% of winter reads against 7% of summer reads (Wilcoxon *p* = 1.9 × 10⁻⁵), and the dark fraction as a whole is 51% of winter against 31% of summer reads. **(C)** The 30 dark OTUs with the highest mean winter read share (Table S-E1b), plotted as prevalence — the number of the 26 winter samples with any detection — against that mean share, coloured as in (A). OTU1369 is labelled: it is winter's single most abundant OTU at 11.2% of winter reads and is present in 20 of 26 winter droppings, yet its best UNITE hit is only 85% similar, so it forms a candidate new Species Hypothesis rather than matching anything named.

Roughly half of a typical winter dropping is reads that the canonical taxonomy cannot name (Section 3.4), and that single label covers two different problems. A little over a third of dark OTUs are near-identical to a UNITE reference and are dark only because `minBoot = 80` declines to commit to a genus at that bootstrap — a cost of conservatism, and one that Species Hypothesis matching largely recovers (of the 390 dark OTUs with a best hit at all, 37% sit at ≥ 99% identity; Figure S-E1a). But a comparable fraction of them (38%) sits below 95% identity, where no threshold adjustment would help, and panel A shows where that leads: 228 of the 493 dark OTUs (46%) form candidate new Species Hypotheses rather than matching an existing one, and a further 103 (21%) have no UNITE reference within 80% identity at all. Two thirds of the unnamed community is therefore unnamed because the reference lacks it, not because the classifier was cautious. Panel B supplies the weight behind that count, and it is strongly seasonal: candidate-novel lineages account for 29% of winter reads but only 7% of summer reads, so winter dung is not merely more dark than summer dung, it is dark in a different way — dominated by lineages with no named counterpart rather than by unnamed relatives of known ones. Panel C locates that signal in individual taxa: the dark OTUs carrying real winter read share are predominantly candidate-novel, and the most extreme of them, OTU1369, is simultaneously the most abundant and among the most prevalent OTUs in winter dung while being only 85% similar to its nearest named relative. One caveat travels with the figure throughout. "Candidate novel" is a statement about the reference database rather than a taxonomic claim: these are unimprinted clusters awaiting public sequence deposition and PlutoF registration (Section 3.4), so none of them yet carries a permanent identifier.
::::

```{r fig3-build}
#| eval: false
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Full build code for Figure 3 — the source of truth for figures/main/Fig3_dark_taxa_SH.{png,jpg,pdf}"

# Figure 3 -- Winter dung is dominated by dark, largely candidate-novel lineages
# (E1). Journal layout: 174 mm double column, 7-8 pt text.
# Every quantity is READ from committed tables/ CSVs written by
# 9_dark_taxa_SH_matching.R (the SH assignment itself is an external containerised
# step, ~90 min) and 8_functional_guilds.R (sample order only):
#   A  tables/E1_SH_readshare_by_sample.csv      per-dropping read share by stratum
#      tables/guild_composition_per_sample.csv   Figure 1's sample order (asserted
#                                                 against Figure 1 inside fig1-build)
#   B  tables/E1_winter_dominant_dark_taxa_SH.csv the 30 dark OTUs with the highest
#                                                 mean winter read share (Table S-E1b)
#   key tables/E1_SH_assignment_summary.csv       OTU counts per placement
# tables/dark_taxa_SH_matching.csv is the per-OTU table all of these derive from;
# it is read as a drift guard.
# Colour grammar shared with Figures 1 and 2: winter BLUE = the dark taxa, here
# split into a lightness ramp by how novel they are (pale = inside a named UNITE
# Species Hypothesis, mid = candidate new SH, deepest = no UNITE relative within
# 80% identity); reads on OTUs with a genus are light grey.
# Rebuild:  conda run -n r_env Rscript build_main_figure.R fig3-build

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2); library(patchwork); library(ggtext)
})
stopifnot(capabilities("cairo"))          # Unicode glyphs need the cairo devices

tab_dir <- if (dir.exists("tables")) "tables" else
           "/home/daniel/Ptarmigan/Scripts_server/Supplementary/tables"
out_dir <- "figures/main"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
grDevices::pdf(NULL)                                  # headless: no X11 fallback

# ---- journal style (as Figures 1 and 2) -------------------------------------
FONT  <- "Liberation Sans"                # metric-identical to Arial
PT    <- function(pt) pt / ggplot2::.pt   # pt -> ggplot text size / linewidth (mm)
FIG_W <- 174; FIG_H <- 138                # mm
INK   <- "grey10"
COL_W <- "#0072B2"; COL_S <- "#D55E00"    # winter / summer (repo standard)

theme_journal <- function() {
  theme_classic(base_size = 7, base_family = FONT) +
    theme(text         = element_text(size = 7, colour = INK, family = FONT),
          axis.text    = element_text(size = 7, colour = INK),
          axis.title   = element_text(size = 8, colour = INK),
          axis.line    = element_line(linewidth = PT(0.5), colour = INK),
          axis.ticks   = element_line(linewidth = PT(0.5), colour = INK),
          axis.ticks.length = unit(1, "mm"),
          legend.text  = element_text(size = 7, colour = INK),
          legend.title = element_text(size = 7, colour = INK),
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          strip.text   = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", colour = INK),
          plot.title   = element_blank(),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7, colour = "grey25"),
          plot.tag     = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", colour = "black"),
          plot.margin  = margin(1, 1, 1, 1, "mm"))
}
# Type audit -- fails the build rather than ship text outside 7-8 pt.
audit <- function(p, id) {
  th <- p$theme
  for (nm in c("axis.text.x", "axis.text.y", "axis.title.x", "axis.title.y", "legend.text",
               "legend.title", "strip.text", "plot.subtitle", "plot.tag")) {
    el <- tryCatch(calc_element(nm, th), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(el) || inherits(el, "element_blank") || !is.numeric(el$size)) next
    if (el$size < 7 - 1e-9 || el$size > 8 + 1e-9)
      stop(sprintf("%s: theme %s = %.2f pt (allowed 7-8)", id, nm, el$size))
  }
  for (i in seq_along(p$layers)) {
    l <- p$layers[[i]]
    if (inherits(l$geom, c("GeomText", "GeomLabel", "GeomRichtext", "GeomRichText",
                           "GeomTextRepel"))) {
      sz <- l$aes_params$size
      if (is.null(sz)) stop(sprintf("%s: layer %d text has no explicit size", id, i))
      if (sz * ggplot2::.pt < 7 - 1e-9 || sz * ggplot2::.pt > 8 + 1e-9)
        stop(sprintf("%s: layer %d text %.2f pt (allowed 7-8)", id, i, sz * ggplot2::.pt))
    }
    lw <- l$aes_params$linewidth
    if (is.numeric(lw) && lw * ggplot2::.pt < 0.25 - 1e-9)
      stop(sprintf("%s: layer %d linewidth %.2f pt < 0.25", id, i, lw * ggplot2::.pt))
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# ---- strata and colours -----------------------------------------------------
# "Candidate new SH" and "no relative" are the SAME kind of outcome -- neither
# falls inside an existing named SH -- and differ only in whether the sequence
# has any UNITE relative at all; the ramp makes them neighbours. no_SH_match and
# the 13 QC-removed OTUs (excluded_nonITS) share the deepest level, as in
# script 9 Section 4b; Section 3.4 keeps them apart.
STRATA <- c("Genus assigned", "Dark: in a named SH", "Dark: candidate new SH",
            "Dark: no relative >= 80%")
STRAT_COLS <- setNames(c("#D9D9D9", "#9CC3E0", COL_W, "#003B5C"), STRATA)
rs_map <- c("Named"                   = STRATA[1],
            "Dark: placeable"         = STRATA[2],
            "Dark: candidate novel"   = STRATA[3],
            "Dark: no reference <80%" = STRATA[4])
sh_class_map <- c(placeable_existing_SH = STRATA[2], novel_new_SH = STRATA[3],
                  no_SH_match = STRATA[4], excluded_nonITS = STRATA[4])
on_dark <- function(cat) cat %in% STRATA[3:4]        # white text on these fills

# ============================================================================
# Panel A -- every dropping's read share by stratum, Figure 1's sample order
# ============================================================================
rs <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "E1_SH_readshare_by_sample.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(rs$stratum %in% names(rs_map)), all(rs$Season %in% c("winter", "summer")),
          length(unique(rs$sample)) == 52L,
          max(abs(tapply(rs$read_share, rs$sample, sum) - 1)) < 1e-6)
rs$cat <- factor(unname(rs_map[rs$stratum]), levels = STRATA)
rs$Season <- factor(c(winter = "Winter", summer = "Summer")[rs$Season],
                    levels = c("Winter", "Summer"))

# Figure 1's order: within season, descending dung-saprotroph share (stable sort
# on the committed table's row order; fig1-build asserts this equals its own).
gc <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "guild_composition_per_sample.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
gc$Season <- factor(gc$Season, levels = c("Winter", "Summer"))
ord <- gc$SampleID[order(gc$Season, -gc[["Dung saprotroph"]])]
stopifnot(setequal(ord, rs$sample), all(table(gc$Season) == 26L))
xpos <- setNames(ave(seq_along(ord), gc$Season[match(ord, gc$SampleID)], FUN = seq_along), ord)
MEAN_X <- 26 + 1 + 2; MEAN_W <- 3

per <- data.frame(sample = rs$sample, Season = rs$Season, cat = rs$cat, share = rs$read_share,
                  x = xpos[rs$sample], w = 1)
mn  <- aggregate(share ~ Season + cat, per, mean)
mn$sample <- "mean"; mn$x <- MEAN_X; mn$w <- MEAN_W
bars <- rbind(per[, names(mn)], mn)
bars <- bars[order(bars$Season, bars$sample, bars$cat), ]
bars$ymax <- ave(bars$share, bars$Season, bars$sample, FUN = cumsum)
bars$ymin <- bars$ymax - bars$share

# Drift guards: the season means must reproduce the per-OTU table's season
# columns, computed independently (script 9 Section 4, not 4b) ...
sh <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "dark_taxa_SH_matching.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(sh) == 1129L, is.logical(sh$is_dark), all(sh$SH_class %in% names(sh_class_map)))
sh$cat <- factor(ifelse(sh$is_dark, unname(sh_class_map[sh$SH_class]), STRATA[1]), levels = STRATA)
for (s in c("Winter", "Summer")) {
  col <- if (s == "Winter") "winter_mean_share" else "summer_mean_share"
  ref <- tapply(sh[[col]], sh$cat, sum)
  got <- setNames(mn$share[mn$Season == s], as.character(mn$cat[mn$Season == s]))
  stopifnot(max(abs(ref[STRATA] - got[STRATA])) < 1e-6)
}
# ... and the numbers the text quotes (Section 3.4 / 2026-09-11 decision).
nov <- per[per$cat == STRATA[3], ]
nov_m <- tapply(100 * nov$share, nov$Season, mean)
nov_p <- wilcox.test(share ~ Season, data = nov)$p.value
stopifnot(round(nov_m[["Winter"]], 1) == 29.2, round(nov_m[["Summer"]], 1) == 7.2,
          signif(nov_p, 2) == 1.9e-05)

lab_mean <- bars[bars$sample == "mean" & bars$share >= 0.05, ]
lab_mean$txt <- sprintf("%.0f", 100 * lab_mean$share)
season_strip <- function(s) sprintf("<span style='color:%s'>**%s**</span>",

strip_lab <- setNames(vapply(c("Winter", "Summer"), season_strip, ""), c("Winter", "Summer"))

pA <- ggplot(bars) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = x - w / 2, xmax = x + w / 2, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = cat),

finest <- function(tx) {
  r <- strsplit(tx, ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  r <- r[!grepl("__$|unidentified|Incertae", r)]
  sub("^[a-z]__", "", r[length(r)])

asum <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "E1_SH_assignment_summary.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
n_otu <- table(sh$cat)[STRATA]
stopifnot(nrow(asum) == 1L, asum$n_dark == sum(sh$is_dark), sum(n_otu[-1]) == asum$n_dark,

pK <- ggplot(key) +

# ---- assemble and write ----------------------------------------------------

# Every main figure is written three ways: PNG and JPG (600 dpi raster, for
# submission systems that demand one or the other) and PDF (vector, for print).
save_fig <- function(stem, obj, width, height, res = 600) {
  one <- function(open_dev) { open_dev(); on.exit(grDevices::dev.off()); print(obj) }
  png_dev <- if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_png else grDevices::png
  one(function() png_dev(paste0(stem, ".png"), width = width, height = height,
                         units = "in", res = res))
  one(function() grDevices::jpeg(paste0(stem, ".jpg"), width = width, height = height,
                                 units = "in", res = res, quality = 95))
  one(function() grDevices::cairo_pdf(paste0(stem, ".pdf"), width = width, height = height))
}
save_fig(file.path(out_dir, "Fig3_dark_taxa_SH"), fig3, FIG_W / 25.4, FIG_H / 25.4)
```

### 10.4 Figure 4 — Pooled versus per-dropping diversity (H2)

:::: {.content-visible when-profile="docs"}
*Provenance: Fig. 4A reads `tables/H2_iNEXT3D_TD_coverage_rarefied_boot.csv` (every rarefaction draw × bootstrap replicate behind Table S8, written by `Scripts/6_diversity_analyses.R` Section 1, which replays iNEXT3D's own bootstrap and checks it against the committed per-draw s.e.) and Table S9 (`tables/H2_season_effect_per_sample.csv`); Fig. 4B reads Table S10's per-sample table (`tables/report_dominance_per_sample.csv`, written by `sec5-build`). Every printed ratio and p is drift-guarded in the chunk. The former four-panel figure, with its full legend and narrative, is Figure S8b (Section 5.5).*
::::

![](figures/main/Fig4_richness_evenness_crossover.png)

**Figure 4**: Pooled across droppings, summer is the richer season at every Hill order; within a single dropping, winter is the more diverse one once abundance is weighted. **(A)** Summer/winter ratio of taxonomic Hill diversity at orders q = 0, 1 and 2 (log scale; the dashed line marks equal diversity). *Pooled season*: iNEXT3D estimates from incidence data, every dropping rarefied to 12,615 reads and both seasons standardised to sample coverage 0.65; points give the median ratio over 50 rarefaction draws (Table S8), and bars the 2.5–97.5% range of the ratio formed within each of the 50 draws × 100 bootstrap replicates. *Single dropping*: year-adjusted summer/winter ratio from a gamma GLM (log link) of the size-standardised per-dropping Hill number on Season + Year (n = 52), with its 95% confidence interval (Table S9). **(B)** Read share of each dropping's single most abundant OTU, by season. Boxes show the median and interquartile range, points are individual droppings, white diamonds are season means, and the bracket gives the Wilcoxon rank-sum test (Table S10). The former four-panel version of this figure is Figure S8b.
